stem: A 15-year-old boy shows significant wear on his upper anterior teeth but no signs of decay. He also has a morning cough and halitosis. What is the most likely cause of this tooth structure loss?

options.text: Extrinsic acid from excessive soft drink consumption.
A neutrophil function defect causing tooth migration.

explanation: The text describes a case where a boy was treated for asthma for a morning cough when the true cause was reflux-induced acid erosion.
rationale: The symptoms of a morning cough and burping after meals suggest a digestive issue.

optionExplanations.A: While possible, the specific combination of a morning cough and halitosis suggests an internal (intrinsic) source of acid.
optionExplanations.B: The text describes a case where a boy was treated for asthma for a morning cough when the true cause was reflux-induced acid erosion.
optionExplanations.C: Neutrophil defects lead to periodontal disease and tooth loss, not the smooth acid erosion of the front teeth.
optionExplanations.D: The text explicitly states that the wear in this example was not from trauma or decay, but erosion.
